source.title: The Interaction Bottleneck of Deep Neural Networks: Discovery, Proof, and Modulation
source.authors: Huiqi Deng; Qi-Han Ren; Zhuo-Fan Chen; Zhenyu Cui; Wen Shen; Peng Zhang; Hong-Bin Pei; Quanshi Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no material cut-off or garbling affecting the extracted results.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports how deliberately modulating interaction orders changes fitting and train–test loss gaps, extending the claim’s generalization topic to a different training setup. It does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper’s interaction-strength distributions and structural-modeling and adversarial-robustness results do not measure the claim’s listed versions. Rows below cover the reported fitting and generalization results. No random-label experiment, width sweep, optimizer or batch-size comparison, dropout comparison, sharpness measure, or memorized-example removal is reported.
record.test_reason: The study measures interaction-order modulation, fitting loss, and train–test loss gaps. None of its comparisons tests V1–V8. Related-work citations to generalization and sharpness do not constitute tests of those versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' interpretation: low-order bias weakens fitting while reducing generalization gaps, high-order bias favors fitting while increasing gaps, and final test accuracies can remain close. However, Table 3 does not show better high-order fitting than normal fitting: training losses are equal on CIFAR-10 and higher on TinyImageNet. Smaller gaps should also be distinguished from higher held-out accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains variants with added encouraging or suppressing interaction-order losses; these are not the claim versions’ standard-training comparisons. The fitting and generalization table uses AlexNet and VGG16 on CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet; the text also describes three-layer MLP experiments on tabular data.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported fitting and generalization pattern varies with interaction-order bias and dataset; Table 3 reports different loss gaps for CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Low-order variants have higher training losses and smaller train–test loss gaps than normal variants in all four architecture–dataset comparisons. High-order variants have larger gaps throughout; their training losses equal normal losses on CIFAR-10 and exceed them on TinyImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicitly suppressing selected interaction orders changes training fit and train–test loss gaps; low-order-biased models show weaker fitting and smaller gaps in these experiments.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (journal header); publication status not stated
record.problems: The fitting and generalization comparisons use deliberately modulated interaction losses, so they do not establish the listed versions under standard training. Table 3 reports results for two architectures and two datasets; uncertainty estimates are not stated. Additional tabular results are described in text and Figure 12 rather than tabulated here.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results left out. Figure 12’s qualitative MLP-8 Commercial training–validation dynamics are not separately rowed because Table 3 supplies the numeric fitting and gap comparisons, and the figure text gives no numeric values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and random-label chance performance.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and tuning-dependent qualifications.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including dataset-size, augmentation, and weight-decay conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The Table 3 extraction misassigns TinyImageNet training-loss entries. The purported conclusion support in E2 reverses low-order and high-order behavior and does not appear in the supplied conclusion. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not imply their reported loss comparisons are unreadable.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
